Issue #187: Dispatch: a review rerun after a failed attempt starts from the plan stage's original output, discarding the owner's revise

## What happened

A plan ticket on a client project reached the review stage's finalize decision and the owner answered `revise` with a note of lead decisions. The reviser wrote the revised plan to `review/1/joined/plan.md` (09:28). The review run then failed with `review run gone: no such run`, and the rerun decision was answered `rerun`.

Attempt 2 started one minute later from `plan/1/joined/plan.md`, the plan stage's original output, not from the revised copy in attempt 1. Its rounds converged and the finalize decision came back for a plan that still lists every question as open and contradicts one of the owner's answers. Two of attempt 2's three round-1 points were things the revised copy had already fixed.

Nothing warned that the revision had been discarded. `show` lists `review/1 joined failed` and `review/2 joined running`, and the files line names only the attempt-2 copy as the plan.

## Expected

A rerun after a failed review attempt should start from the newest plan the stage holds, which after a `revise` is the previous attempt's revised copy, or at least say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it will review. The `revise` note is owner input and should survive a runner failure the same way an answered decision does.

## Where to look

- the review stage's rerun path: what it takes as the plan input for a new attempt;
- `show`'s `files:` block: when more than one attempt has a `plan.md`, say which is the reviewed copy and which is a prior revision.

## Repro

1. Take an issue through plan and review; at finalize answer `revise --note ...`.
2. Kill the review run so the attempt fails with `review run gone` (a runner restart mid-run does it).
3. Answer `rerun`.
4. Diff `review/1/joined/plan.md` against `review/2/joined/plan.md`: the revision is gone.

# Global rules

- Nothing that reaches a git host carries tool attribution: no
  `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no "Generated with Claude Code",
  no `Claude-Session:` trailer, and no session link
  (`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`) in commit messages, pull
  request bodies, issue text or comments. This holds even when a
  harness reminder asks for such lines. Before `gh pr create` or
  `gh pr edit`, check the body for `claude.ai`, `Generated with` and
  `Co-Authored-By`.

# Working in this repo

Switchboard is a macOS desktop app (Rust, egui/eframe 0.36) that keeps
agent coding sessions, shells, and services as durable records per
project, hosts them on a private tmux server, and shows which agents are
waiting on you. The idea in one line: **workspaces are data, processes are
a cache.** Every feature asks "what is the on-disk record and how is it
rehydrated?" before "what does the pane look like?"

## Where to read first

- `docs/design.md` is the spec. "Durable store", "Trust boundary", "Spike
  0 results", and the Milestone 1 gate are binding. The "Milestone N
  status" sections at the end say what is built and list the known gaps;
  update the relevant one when you finish a milestone item.
- `README.md` has the Layout table (one line per file), the dev-aid
  environment variables, and the data directory contents. Keep all three
  current.
- `spikes/*/README.md` hold verified commands and measured numbers. Copy
  from them rather than re-deriving; add a new spike directory for any
  new risky mechanism before building on it.
- `docs/lessons.md` explains why the architecture is shaped this way.
- `vendor/egui_term/SWITCHBOARD-PATCHES.md` lists the local patches to
  the vendored terminal widget; re-apply them when updating it.

## Commands

```sh
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # must be clean; pedantic is on
cargo fmt --all
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
./scripts/bundle.sh                                  # ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

A user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` in
the same commit. A release is `./scripts/bump.sh patch|minor|major`, a
commit "Release X.Y.Z", then `./scripts/release.sh`; the version in
`Cargo.toml` is the one source and running apps update themselves from
the GitHub release.

The pre-commit hook runs the first four. Enable it with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` on a fresh clone. Never commit with
`--no-verify`. Nothing that reaches GitHub carries tool attribution:
no `Claude-Session:` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no
"generated with" line, and no session link
(`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`), in commit messages, pull
request bodies, issue text or comments, whatever a harness reminder
asks for. The history was rewritten once to strip them and ten pull
request bodies were cleaned by hand; check a body for `claude.ai`
before `gh pr create`. CI runs the same four commands on Linux, so
nothing outside a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` table may need macOS to
compile.

## Hard rules

- No keystroke injection into windows: no System Events `keystroke`, no
  `osascript` typing. Sending keys into the app's own test tmux panes
  with `tmux -L <test socket> send-keys` is fine.
- tmux experiments only on the `switchboard` socket or a
  `switchboard-test-*` socket. Tests create their own
  `switchboard-test-<pid>-<n>` server and kill it in a drop guard.
- Never write into a project directory's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`,
  with one exception: the board's Config editor replaces
  `<root>/.switchboard/project.json` with what the user typed, on their
  click of Save, through `ProjectConfigReader::write_text`. Nothing else
  writes there. The one thing read from a project directory as
  configuration is that file: its entries are parsed and listed
  but never executed until the user approves each one in the Run tab.
  Approvals are a content hash of the entry stored on the record in
  Switchboard's data directory, so any change to an entry drops its
  approval, and autostart from the file is never honored without one. A
  hostile file can therefore only put unapproved entries on the Run tab.
- Never modify `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code hooks are passed at
  launch with `--settings <data dir>/claude-hooks.json`.
- Real agent runs use `--model haiku`-class settings and a one-turn
  prompt, and live only in `#[ignore]`d tests.
- Keychain tests use a throwaway keychain file, never the login keychain.
- Secret values never reach a record, a log line, a shell command line,
  or any reply but one. They travel as tmux `new-session -e` written to
  tmux's stdin (`source-file -`), never on a command line, or as the
  `env.resolve` reply on `control.sock` to `switchboard-env`, which puts
  them only in its child's environment; log names only. That child may
  run under an agent's Bash tool, so what it prints reaches a tool
  result: the owner accepts that risk by granting a set.
- Agents are never resumed automatically (a resume costs money). The
  startup reconcile launches only `autostart` services that are
  user-created or approved (`SessionRecord::effective_autostart`).
- Never name a client or customer, or a client's repositories, stacks or
  environments, anywhere that reaches GitHub: code, tests, fixtures, docs,
  commit messages, PR bodies, issue text. Say "the client project" or "a
  pipeline". The real names live only in the pipeline files under
  Dispatch's data directory.

## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## Extending the contract

- `src/core/model.rs`, `src/core/action.rs` (`AppAction`/`Effect`), and
  `src/ports/` are the shared contract. Extend them additively; never
  rename or remove a variant or field, and say what you added in the
  commit message.
- A change to any type in `model.rs` that is serialized needs a
  `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Readers
  accept older versions; the store refuses to write a newer one.
- Writes to records go through the store's atomic path (temp file,
  fsync, `.bak`, rename). Never write a record file any other way.

## Adding a feature

1. Action variant plus core transition plus a core test in
   `src/core/tests.rs`.
2. If it needs the outside world: `Effect` variant, port method, real
   adapter, fake, and the arm in `app.rs` that runs it.
3. Widget under `src/ui/` and a UI test in `tests/ui.rs`.
4. A `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line in `src/script.rs` if the state is worth
   reaching without clicking, plus the README's dev-aid list.
5. README Layout table for any new file; design.md status section for
   any milestone item.

## Driving the live app

There is no keystroke injection. Put the running app into a state with
`SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT=<file>` (one action per line, see `src/script.rs`)
while `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` point at test
locations, then screenshot the window with `screencapture -l <window
id>`. Keep the data dir path short: the wake socket path has a 104-byte
limit. Hook events can be injected by running `switchboard-hook <EventName>`
by hand with the hook JSON on stdin and `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_ID` and
`SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` set, for example
`echo '{"error":"rate_limit"}' | switchboard-hook StopFailure` or
`echo '{"tool_name":"AskUserQuestion"}' | switchboard-hook PermissionRequest`.

## Testing rules

- Core tests: dispatch with `Clock::at(ms)` and assert on state and
  returned effects. Never sleep.
- UI tests (`tests/ui.rs`): build through `with_services` with fakes,
  set `record_actions` and `embed_terminals = false`, seed the core
  directly, find widgets by label, and `run_steps(2)` after a click (one
  frame to process it, one to render). `type_text` only sends a Text
  event; call `.focus()` on the node first. Size the harness tall enough
  that everything you click is on screen. Assert on `dispatched` for

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. ## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## What happened

A plan ticket on a client project reached the review stage's finalize decision and the owner answered `revise` with a note of lead decisions. ## Expected

A rerun after a failed review attempt should start from the newest plan the stage holds, which after a `revise` is the previous attempt's revised copy, or at least say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it will review. The `revise` note is owner input and should survive a runner failure the same way an answered decision does.

- the review stage's rerun path: what it takes as the plan input for a new attempt;
- `show`'s `files:` block: when more than one attempt has a `plan.md`, say which is the reviewed copy and which is a prior revision.

1. Take an issue through plan and review; at finalize answer `revise --note ...`.
2. Kill the review run so the attempt fails with `review run gone` (a runner restart mid-run does it).
3. Answer `rerun`.
4. Diff `review/1/joined/plan.md` against `review/2/joined/plan.md`: the revision is gone.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

1	# Investigation notes: issue #187 (review rerun discards the revised plan)
2	
3	Worktree: `/Users/sully/code_repos/plan-trial/sb-187-stage-investigate-v5-sonnet-b`. Line numbers are from this tree.
4	Read: CLAUDE.md, docs/lessons.md (generic Prompt Box lessons, nothing on Dispatch), the design.md "Plan review workflow" section (line 1000) and the Dispatch sections around lines 1775-1800, and docs/dispatch.md (decisions 6 and 16 at ~3170-3215, failure rules at ~2490-2510, the test table at ~2975 and ~3078).
5	I did not read all 3678 lines of design.md.
6	The issue is in the `dispatch/` crate, not the egui app. The egui app only hosts the workflow run (`src/core/control.rs:1384`, `ControlAction::StartWorkflow` at `src/core/control.rs:125`).
7	
8	## On-disk record, then rehydration (before any pane or CLI output)
9	
10	The ticket record is `<data>/.../tickets/<id>` (`Ticket` in `dispatch/src/ticket.rs`). Saved through `save_ticket`.
11	- A workflow attempt (`AttemptKind::Workflow`) is an `Attempt` in `t.attempts`. Its `artifacts` map holds one entry, `subject -> <attempt_dir>/<subject>.md`, e.g. `review/1/joined/plan.md`.
12	  - The directory comes from `attempt_dir` (`scheduler.rs:6303`): `<ticket_dir>/<stage>/<n>/<ctx>`.
13	  - `start_workflow` creates that copy with `std::fs::copy` of the source plan (`scheduler.rs:7436-7500`, copy at ~7469).
14	- The review run edits that copy in place. The planner clone applies accepted points to it.
15	- Round files sit beside the copy: `<stem>.feedback-<n>.md` and `<stem>.response-<n>.md` (`report.rs:156-210`).
16	- `revise` (`scheduler.rs:7565`) does these things:
17	  - It writes the owner's note as the next round's feedback file, headed `OWNER_ROUND_HEADING`.
18	  - It pushes `Revision{round,by,at_ms}` onto `attempt.revisions` (`ticket.rs:510`).
19	  - It sends `Body::WorkflowObject` to the app.
20	- The note is also kept on the decision. `DecisionState::Answered{note,by,..}` stays in `t.decisions`, and the `Answered` event is in the event log. This is how "an answered decision survives" today.
21	- The only copy of the revised plan is the file in `review/1/joined/`. The ticket record holds just its path.
22	
23	When the run fails:
24	- `poll_workflow` (`scheduler.rs:7740-7765`) gets `NO_SUCH_RUN` (`scheduler.rs:8445`) and calls `fail_attempt(.., "review run gone: no such run")`.
25	- That reaches `fail_attempt_with` (`scheduler.rs:7195`). The attempt becomes `AttemptState::Failed`, it is saved, and a `rerun` decision is asked via `ensure_decision` / `ask_rerun` (`scheduler.rs:7308`).
26	- `rerun_ask` (`scheduler.rs:9335`) builds the question text. For a Workflow attempt `rerun_carries` (`scheduler.rs:9382`) returns `""`, so the question says nothing about which plan the rerun reviews.
27	- The existing test `a_run_switchboard_no_longer_has_fails_the_attempt` is at `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3809`.
28	
29	Rehydration after the `rerun` answer:
30	- `rerun` is acted on at `scheduler.rs:3524` (`("rerun","rerun")` calls `rerun_note` and `retire_replaced`). The workflow lane is then relaunched by `may_rerun` at `scheduler.rs:7402` and `7421`. Both call `start_workflow` with `next_n`.
31	- `rerun_note` (`scheduler.rs:8988`) returns `None` unless the stage kind is `Agent` or `Review`. The code-review kind `StageKind::Review` is what the code calls "Review". A `Workflow` stage returns `None`, so a note on a workflow `rerun` goes nowhere.
32	- **Root cause:** `review_subject` (`scheduler.rs:10534`) picks the source plan.
33	  - It walks `t.attempts` newest first and keeps only `state == Complete` attempts that have `artifacts[subject]`.
34	  - The failed `review/1` is not Complete, so it is skipped. The result is `plan/1/joined/plan.md` plus plan/1's session as `source`.
35	  - Repro line `review/1/joined/plan.md -> review/2/joined/plan.md` is then a copy of the original plan.
36	  - `review/1/joined/plan.md` is left on disk, still holding the revision, and nothing points to it except the old failed attempt's `artifacts`.
37	- The same exclusion is asserted on purpose in the `shown` test, `ticket.rs:1850-1866`: "A parked review's copy is not the plan going forward" for Failed and Cancelled. Any fix has to be reconciled with that test and with `input_where` (`ticket.rs:1452`).
38	  - `input`/`input_where` (`ticket.rs:1437-1462`) feed later agent stages and also require Complete.
39	  - The comment on `shown_where` says "an agent is handed `input_where`'s complete files".
40	- `source_session` is the same `a.session` of the plan attempt (`review_subject` returns it). The run clones that planner's transcript (design.md ~1000-1050). A rerun from a revised copy would still clone the original planner, which never saw the revision exchange. The tree does not say what that implies for the clone's behaviour.
41	
42	## What the user sees (after the above)
43	
44	- `show` -> `ticket_paths` (`serve.rs:~545`) builds `plan_files` from `shown_lane_files(t,p,"plan")` (`scheduler.rs:10900`, `lane_files_by` at 10908), which calls `Ticket::shown_where` (`ticket.rs:1476`).
45	  - `shown_where` keeps `Complete` attempts plus open Workflow attempts only.
46	  - With `review/1` Failed and `review/2` open, only `review/2`'s copy is returned. `LaneFile{reviewing, round}` (`serve.rs:~548`, `review_round` at ~527) is computed for that one file.
47	  - `main.rs:~895-908` `print_lane_files` prints `plan: <path>` and `(reviewed copy, round N, review open)`.
48	  - There is no output that names a superseded or prior revised copy, and none that says what attempt 2 was built from. The `attempts` list shows `review/1 joined failed` and `review/2 joined running` (the issue's wording), with no link between them.
49	- The `rerun` question text (`rerun_ask`, `scheduler.rs:9335`; and the `fail_attempt_with` version at 7263) names no plan.
50	- `finalize` question (`review_done`, `scheduler.rs:7690`) says "The reviewed copy is {copy}", which is the only place a path is named.
51	- `report.rs` `plan_review` (~340) and `serve.rs` `plan_rounds` (~500) read round files per workflow attempt from `a.artifacts.values().next()`. Attempt 1's rounds (including the owner's round) will still appear under attempt 1.
52	
53	## What the issue asks, and what the tree gives
54	
55	- Expected: rerun starts from the newest plan the stage holds, or at least says which copy it reviews in the rerun question and in `show`. The `revise` note should survive a runner failure like an answered decision does.
56	- The note itself already survives: it is on the decision (`Answered.note`), in `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-2.md`, and in `attempt.revisions`. What does not survive is the effect of the note (the revised copy) as the next attempt's input.
57	- Nothing in the tree currently records "this attempt's input came from X". `new_attempt(..)` (called at `scheduler.rs:~7480`) takes only the artifacts map. There is no field for the source path on `Attempt`. `Attempt` has `carried_from` for code review only (design.md ~1795).
58	- Adding a field to `Attempt`/`Ticket` means the record version rule in CLAUDE.md applies for Switchboard's `model.rs`; for Dispatch it is `RECORD_VERSION` (design.md ~1799 mentions "dispatch `RECORD_VERSION` 4") and `store.rs` migrations (`store.rs:~518-547`). I did not read the version or migrate code in full.
59	
60	## Tests near the change
61	
62	- `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs`: `at_finalize`, `at_review_run`, `revise`, `artifact_of` helpers; `revise_writes_the_owners_round...` at 3442; `a_run_switchboard_no_longer_has_fails_the_attempt` at 3809. A test for this issue would drive: finalize, `revise`, then clear `env.sb().runs`, step, answer `rerun`, step, and compare which `plan` file `WorkflowStart` got. The fake Switchboard in `dispatch/tests/support` records `runs` and `objections`.
63	- `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:1836-1905` covers `shown` / `input` rules.
64	- `scheduler.rs:12838-12869` has the "finalized: next stage follows the reviewed copy" tests.
65	- Per CLAUDE.md a user-visible change needs a CHANGELOG.md Unreleased line, and README/design status updates. CLAUDE.md's Dispatch guidance is mostly for the app; Dispatch's own spec is `docs/dispatch.md`, which has the test tables and decision list (item 16, "A review runs on a copy of the reviewed artifact").
66	
67	## Not checked
68	
69	- I did not run anything: no tests, no reproduction.
70	- I did not read `retire_replaced`, `next_n`, `latest_attempt`, `may_rerun` bodies, `new_attempt`, `Attempt` field list, or `store.rs` migration code.
71	- I did not check other callers of `review_subject` or of `input`/`input_where` for other stages that could take a failed review's copy (e.g. a code-review or a later stage reading `plan`).
72	- I did not check how `restart`, `park`, or `resume` interact with a failed review attempt's copy (the `Cancelled` case in `ticket.rs:1850` is deliberate).
73	- I did not check the app side (`ControlAction::StartWorkflow` at `src/core/control.rs:441`) for what it does with a plan path or source session on a second run in the same ticket.
74	- I did not check the claim that attempt 2's round-1 points were "things the revised copy had already fixed" beyond the code path above; that is the issue's account of a client ticket.
75	
76	## Open questions
77	
78	- [tree] What does `StartWorkflow` in the app (`src/core/control.rs:441`, the workflow start in `src/core/`) do with `source` and `plan`: does it read the plan from the path given, clone the planner from `source` at its transcript end, and would a plan newer than that transcript change the clone's behaviour?
79	- [tree] Which other callers use `review_subject`, `input`, `input_where` or `shown_where` for a Workflow stage's subject, and would a change to "newest plan the stage holds" alter what a later stage, a restart, or `forgotten` handling reads?
80	- [tree] Does the failed review attempt's copy and round files remain on disk through `retire_replaced`, `restart`, the close, and any sweep (so a rerun could still read `review/1/joined/plan.md`)?
81	- [tree] How are `Attempt` fields added and versioned in Dispatch (`RECORD_VERSION`, `store.rs` migrate), if the plan needs to record which copy an attempt reviewed?
82	- [tree] Does a `rerun` question's `--note` on a Workflow stage have any consumer today (`rerun_note` returns `None` for a non-Agent/Review kind), and what does the CLI/port do with a note there?
83	- [run] Does the failed `review/1` copy actually contain the revised plan in the issue's flow, i.e. does the planner clone write its edits into the `plan` path given (the copy) rather than elsewhere, and is the file complete when the run is gone mid-round? What is lost is the revised copy as the next attempt's input. The plan changes nothing about how the note is stored.

- **"Or at least say which copy it will review."** Both are done: the seed is chosen, and the `rerun` question and `show` say which copy it is.

This is the "For the owner" line in the facts file. The plan's default is the design that works either way: seed the file, and say in the question that the planner's earlier rounds are not carried. `Attempt` gains `seeded_from: Option<(String, u32)>`, `#[serde(default)]`, next to `carried_from` (`ticket.rs:317`) and written the same way: set when the attempt is made, never changed.
